The factor is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{f(1)}{f(0)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mn>9</mn><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{9}{6}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 1.5</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Rewrite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = 2^{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math> in the form <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(2)^x</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: Exponents add when powers multiply: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{x + 3} = 2^x \cdot 2^3</annotation></semantics></math>, a product, not a sum.

The constant is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^3 = 8</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^3 = 2 \cdot 2 \cdot 2 = 8</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \cdot 3</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: The graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = 2^{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math> is the graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2^x</annotation></semantics></math> shifted <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math> units left. Which other transformation of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y = 2^x</annotation></semantics></math> gives the same graph?
options: A vertical dilation by a factor of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>
A vertical dilation by a factor of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>
A horizontal dilation by a factor of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(-1)</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That reads <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> as <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-2</annotation></semantics></math>. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">8 \cdot 2^{-1} = 8 \cdot \frac{1}{2} = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>4</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(1) = 2^4</annotation></semantics></math>; the input here is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which expressions are equivalent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(x) = 2^{x + 3}</annotation></semantics></math>? Select all that apply.

The table fits <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = 5(4)^x</annotation></semantics></math>. Rewrite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x)</annotation></semantics></math> with base <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>, in the form <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a(2)^{kx}</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 \cdot 4 \cdot 2^x</annotation></semantics></math>, a shift. Changing the base multiplies the exponent: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2^2)^x = 2^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>.

This doubles the outputs once; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> multiplies by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math> each step.

A power of a power multiplies exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2^2)^x = 2^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{x/2}</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which expression is equivalent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x) = 5(4)^x</annotation></semantics></math>?

Find <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)</annotation></semantics></math> exactly.

mistakes.why: That is halfway between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">20</annotation></semantics></math>. An exponential multiplies: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^{1/2} = 2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That multiplies by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the exponent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{2}</annotation></semantics></math> is a square root.

items.q: Which statement about <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x - 1)</annotation></semantics></math> is correct?
options: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>5</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>4</mn><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(x - 1) = \frac{5}{4}(4)^x</annotation></semantics></math>: shifting right <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> divides every output by <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>

items.q: Rewrite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)^x</annotation></semantics></math> as a power of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: A negative exponent is a reciprocal, not a negative number: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{-x}</annotation></semantics></math>, with the minus in the exponent.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{1}{3} = 3^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math>, so the exponent is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1 \cdot x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Rewrite <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{3x}</annotation></semantics></math> in the form <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b^x</annotation></semantics></math>.

form.say: one number to the power x, b^x

mistakes.why: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^3 = 8</annotation></semantics></math>, not <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2 \cdot 3</annotation></semantics></math>.
An exponent of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3x</annotation></semantics></math> multiplies; it does not add.

items.q: Write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{4^{x + 1}}{2^x}</annotation></semantics></math> as a single power of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.

mistakes.why: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>4</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4^{x + 1}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{2(x + 1)}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 2^{2x + 2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the whole exponent doubles.

Dividing subtracts exponents: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 2 - x</annotation></semantics></math>.

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4 = 2^2</annotation></semantics></math>, so the exponent <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x + 1</annotation></semantics></math> doubles to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2x + 2</annotation></semantics></math> before you subtract <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: If <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^x = 7</annotation></semantics></math>, what is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{x + 2}</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That adds <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math>. Adding to the exponent multiplies the power: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn><mo>⋅</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7 \cdot 3^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That squares <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>7</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">7</annotation></semantics></math>; <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>3</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>⋅</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3^{x + 2} = 3^x \cdot 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: If <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^x = 2</annotation></semantics></math>, what is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^{2x}</annotation></semantics></math>?

mistakes.why: That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo>⋅</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5 \cdot 2</annotation></semantics></math>. A power of a power: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^{2x} = (5^x)^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

That is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5^2</annotation></semantics></math>. Use the given value: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(5^x)^2 = 2^2</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Which is equivalent to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>25</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25^{x/2}</annotation></semantics></math>?

A student writes <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^{x + 3} = 2^x + 8</annotation></semantics></math>. Which check shows the error?
options: At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 0</annotation></semantics></math>: both sides equal <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">9</annotation></semantics></math>, so the forms agree

At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^6 = 64</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mn>2</mn><mn>3</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>64</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2^3 + 8 = 64</annotation></semantics></math>, so the forms agree

items.q: Write <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6^x}{2^x}</annotation></semantics></math> as a single power.

mistakes.why: The exponents are equal, but they do not cancel: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><msup><mn>6</mn><mi>x</mi></msup><msup><mn>2</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{6^x}{2^x}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \left(\frac{6}{2}\right)^x</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3^x</annotation></semantics></math>. At <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x = 2</annotation></semantics></math> it is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mn>36</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{36}{4} = 9</annotation></semantics></math>.

Divide the bases, do not subtract them: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mfrac><mn>6</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mi>x</mi></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>3</mn><mi>x</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left(\frac{6}{2}\right)^x = 3^x</annotation></semantics></math>.

items.q: Use exponential regression to model <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>D</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>a</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mi>t</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D(t) = ab^t</annotation></semantics></math>. What is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, correct to three decimal places?
